title: Hybrid connectivity
oneLiner: VPN is quick, cheap and encrypted. Direct Connect is steady and fast but takes weeks and isn't encrypted. Land on a VGW for one VPC, a Transit Gateway for many, and a DX Gateway for many regions.

notes.html: Two ways in from on-premises. Pick by how soon, how steady and whether it must be encrypted.

head: Site-to-Site VPN
Direct Connect (DX)
rows: Private fiber through a DX location
~1.25 Gbps per tunnel, 2 tunnels per connection

items: Several tunnels on a Transit Gateway with ECMP
"branch offices talk to each other through AWS"

notes.text: Where it lands: VGW vs Transit Gateway vs DX Gateway

notes.html: The connection has to end on something on the AWS side. The rule: one VPC → VGW. Many VPCs → Transit Gateway. Many regions over DX → Direct Connect Gateway.

notes.caption: From your router to the right AWS landing point

Regional hub for many VPCs, VPNs and DX
Lets one DX reach VPCs in many regions
To a VGW, or to a DX Gateway

To AWS public endpoints (S3, DynamoDB public IPs) over DX

items: A DX Gateway is not a hub between VPCs. VPCs attached to the same DX Gateway can't talk to each other through it. For VPC-to-VPC, use a Transit Gateway.
Many VPCs over one DX: transit VIF → DX Gateway → Transit Gateway. Not one private VIF per VPC.
A VGW is per VPC and per region. It can't reach a second VPC.

notes.html: DX is private but not encrypted. When a question says compliance needs encryption in transit, add encryption on top.

questions.q: A company with one VPC needs a connection to its data center this week. Traffic must be encrypted and costs kept low. What should they set up?

options.t: Direct Connect with a private VIF
options.why: Takes weeks to provision and isn't encrypted.

options.t: Site-to-Site VPN from a customer gateway to a virtual private gateway
options.why: Right. Up in hours, IPsec-encrypted, one VPC means a VGW.

options.t: VPC peering to the data center
options.why: Peering connects VPCs, not on-premises networks.

options.t: A Transit Gateway with Direct Connect
options.why: Overkill for one VPC, and DX still takes weeks.

questions.q: A company has 40 VPCs in one region and a data center. Every VPC must reach on-premises, and VPCs must reach each other. What should the on-premises VPN terminate on?

options.t: A virtual private gateway in each VPC
options.why: 40 VPNs, and it doesn't solve VPC-to-VPC.

options.t: A Transit Gateway with all 40 VPCs attached
options.why: Right. One VPN to the hub, transitive routing to every VPC.
DX Gateway works only with DX, and it doesn't route VPC-to-VPC.
The customer gateway represents the on-premises router.

questions.q: A company has one Direct Connect connection in us-east-1 and needs private access to VPCs in us-east-1, eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-2. What is the most cost-effective approach?

options.t: Order a Direct Connect connection in each region
options.why: Expensive and slow. Not needed.

options.t: Use a Direct Connect Gateway associated with the VGWs in each region
options.why: Right. One DX reaches VPCs in many regions through the global DX Gateway.

options.t: VPC peering from us-east-1 to the other regions
options.why: Peering isn't transitive, so on-prem traffic can't pass through.
Works, but loses DX's consistent performance. The question asks to use DX.

questions.q: A bank uses Direct Connect. A new rule says all traffic between the data center and AWS must be encrypted in transit. What is the simplest way to meet this with the existing DX?

options.t: DX is encrypted by default, so nothing is needed
options.why: DX is private, not encrypted.

options.t: Run a Site-to-Site VPN over the Direct Connect connection
options.why: Right. IPsec on top of the private line.
There is no such setting.
CloudFront is for HTTP content delivery to users.

questions.q: A company uses a transit VIF on Direct Connect. They want 20 VPCs in two regions reachable from on-premises, with VPC-to-VPC routing controlled centrally. Which design fits?

options.t: Transit VIF → Direct Connect Gateway → a Transit Gateway in each region
options.why: Right. That's the supported path for many VPCs over DX.

options.t: Transit VIF directly to each VPC's VGW
options.why: Transit VIFs connect to a DX Gateway associated with Transit Gateways, not VGWs.
Doesn't scale and gives no VPC-to-VPC routing.

options.t: Direct Connect Gateway alone, which routes between the VPCs
options.why: A DX Gateway doesn't route VPC-to-VPC traffic.

questions.q: Two VPCs in different regions are both associated with the same Direct Connect Gateway. Can instances in VPC A reach VPC B through it?

options.t: Yes, DX Gateway routes between associated VPCs
options.why: It doesn't. It only connects on-prem to the VPCs.

options.t: No. Use a Transit Gateway (with inter-region peering) or VPC peering for VPC-to-VPC
options.why: Right. DX Gateway is not a transit hub between VPCs.

options.t: Yes, if both use the same CIDR
options.why: Overlapping CIDRs would make things worse, not better.
VIF type doesn't change this.

questions.q: A company needs maximum resiliency for its Direct Connect connectivity to AWS for critical workloads. What should they do?

options.t: One DX connection with two VIFs
options.why: Still one physical connection and one location.

options.t: Two DX connections terminating at two different DX locations
options.why: Right. Survives the loss of a device, connection or whole location.

options.t: One DX connection and a NAT gateway
options.why: NAT has nothing to do with on-prem connectivity.
Still a single physical path.

questions.q: A company has a single DX connection and wants a backup path if it fails, at the lowest cost. What should they add?

options.t: A second DX connection at the same location
options.why: Costly, and it shares the location as a failure point.
Right. Cheap, quick, and takes over if DX fails.
Not a network backup path.
Same single point of failure.

questions.q: A Site-to-Site VPN to a Transit Gateway keeps hitting about 1.25 Gbps. The company needs more throughput over VPN. What should they do?

options.t: Increase the VPN tunnel size in the console
options.why: There's no such setting. A tunnel tops out around 1.25 Gbps.

options.t: Create several VPN connections to the Transit Gateway and enable ECMP
options.why: Right. Equal-cost multipath spreads traffic over many tunnels.

options.t: Switch the VPN to a VGW
options.why: VGWs don't support ECMP across VPN connections the way TGW does.
Unrelated to VPN bandwidth.

questions.q: A company signed a Direct Connect order but the circuit needs eight weeks. The migration starts next week and needs private, encrypted connectivity now. What should they do?

options.why: The migration can't wait.

options.t: Set up a Site-to-Site VPN now, then move to DX when it is ready (keeping VPN as backup)
options.why: Right. VPN is up in hours.

options.t: Use VPC peering with the data center
options.why: Peering is VPC-to-VPC only.
That's for S3 uploads over the internet, not network connectivity.

questions.q: On-premises DNS servers must resolve records in a Route 53 private hosted zone associated with a VPC. What should be configured?

options.why: Right. On-prem forwards queries into the VPC through it.
Outbound is for AWS resolving on-prem names.
Exposes internal names to the internet.
Unrelated to DNS resolution.

questions.q: EC2 instances must resolve hostnames in the corp.local domain hosted on on-premises DNS servers. What should be configured?

options.why: Inbound is for on-prem asking about AWS names.

options.t: An outbound endpoint with a forwarding rule for corp.local
options.why: Right. AWS forwards those queries to the on-prem DNS servers.

options.t: A private hosted zone named corp.local
options.why: That would shadow the on-prem domain instead of asking it.
A public resolver can't see corp.local.

questions.q: Branch offices in four cities each have a VPN to AWS. They now need to communicate with each other through AWS using the existing VPNs. What feature fits?

options.why: Right. Hub-and-spoke between branches over a VGW.
That's for DX, not VPN between branches.
Branches aren't VPCs.
Exposes services, not site-to-site routing.

questions.q: Which component represents the on-premises side of a Site-to-Site VPN in AWS?

options.why: That's the AWS side.
Right. AWS's record of your router's public IP.
AWS-side hub.
AWS-side, DX only.

questions.q: On-premises applications must call SQS over an existing Site-to-Site VPN using private IP addresses only. What should be created in the VPC?

options.why: SQS has no gateway endpoint, and gateway endpoints can't be reached from on-prem anyway.
Right. Private IPs in the subnet, reachable over VPN/DX.
On-prem traffic doesn't use the VPC's NAT to reach AWS APIs.
A VIF is for DX, and this is a VPN.

questions.q: A company needs consistent, low-latency, high-throughput connectivity for nightly 20 TB transfers between its data center and AWS. What should they choose?

options.why: Internet-based, so latency and throughput vary.
Right. Dedicated bandwidth and consistent latency.
Snowball is for one-off offline transfers, not nightly jobs.
Still the public internet.

questions.q: Which TWO statements about Direct Connect are true?

options.why: DX is private, not encrypted.

options.t: It can take weeks to provision
options.why: Right.

options.t: A public VIF reaches AWS public services such as S3
options.why: Right.

options.t: It is set up in minutes from the console
options.why: The physical cross-connect takes weeks.

options.t: A Direct Connect Gateway routes traffic between VPCs
options.why: It doesn't route VPC-to-VPC.

questions.q: A company uses a single VPC and Direct Connect. They now add a second VPC in the same region. What is the simplest way to reach both VPCs over the same DX connection?

options.t: A Direct Connect Gateway with a private VIF, associated with both VPCs' VGWs
options.why: Right. One private VIF to the DX Gateway reaches several VGWs.

options.t: Peer the second VPC to the first
options.why: On-prem traffic can't pass through a peering (not transitive).

options.t: A NAT gateway in the first VPC
options.why: Unrelated.
That's for VPN, and doesn't help DX reach another VPC.

questions.q: Which encryption option runs at layer 2 on dedicated 10 or 100 Gbps Direct Connect links?

options.why: IPsec is layer 3, used by VPN over DX.
Right. Layer 2 encryption on supported dedicated connections.
Application layer, inside each connection, not the link.
KMS manages keys for data at rest.

questions.q: An on-premises app must reach an internal ALB in a VPC that is connected through a Transit Gateway, and the app also needs to resolve the ALB's private DNS name. What TWO things are needed?

options.t: A route from on-prem to the VPC CIDR through the TGW attachment
options.why: Right. Traffic needs a path.
Right. On-prem DNS forwards the query into the VPC.
The ALB is internal.
Unrelated to ALBs.
Not needed for internal access.
